title: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose
subject: toxicology
summary: Measure paracetamol at 4 hours or later and plot on the nomogram (US/Canada treatment line 150 mg/L, UK line 100 mg/L at 4 hours). Give IV acetylcysteine (at least 300 mg/kg over 20 to 24 hours, or the 12-hour SNAP regimen) ideally within 8 hours, and continue until stopping criteria are met.

sections.title: Risk assessment
items: Early symptoms are minimal (nausea, vomiting); liver injury appears at 24 to 72 hours. A well-looking patient may still need treatment.
Acetylcysteine is nearly 100% protective if started within 8 hours of ingestion; benefit falls with delay but it is still given after 24 hours if there is evidence of toxicity.

Assess all self-harm ingestions. UK: 75 mg/kg or more in under 1 hour or in any 24 hours needs assessment. US/Canada: start acetylcysteine empirically for more than 200 mg/kg or 10 g if the level will not be back within 8 hours of ingestion.

Staggered ingestion: tablets taken over more than 1 hour. Repeated supratherapeutic ingestion (US): multiple ingestions over more than 24 hours. The nomogram cannot be used in either, or when the time of ingestion is unknown or unreliable.
Massive ingestion: 30 g or more, or a level at or above the 300 mg/L (at 4 hours) line; may cause early coma and lactic acidosis.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Paracetamol level at 4 hours after ingestion, or on arrival if later. A level taken before 4 hours cannot be plotted. Units: mg/L equals mcg/mL.
Baseline ALT (or AST), INR, creatinine, glucose, electrolytes, phosphate and a blood gas with lactate.
If an opioid or anticholinergic was co-ingested and the 4 to 24 hour level is above 10 mg/L but below the line, repeat the level 4 to 6 hours later (US/Canada consensus).
Extended-release paracetamol: repeat the level 4 to 6 hours after the first and treat if either is above the line.

sections.title: Who needs acetylcysteine
items: Single ingestion with a known time, level 4 to 24 hours after ingestion: treat if on or above the treatment line. US/Canada line starts at 150 mg/L at 4 hours; UK (MHRA 2012) single line starts at 100 mg/L at 4 hours. Use one nomogram consistently.
Start acetylcysteine immediately, without waiting for the level, if presenting 8 hours or more after a potentially toxic ingestion, or if the result will not be available within 8 hours of ingestion.
Staggered or uncertain-time ingestion: UK practice is to treat regardless of the level; also treat if ALT or INR is newly abnormal.
Repeated supratherapeutic ingestion (US/Canada): treat if paracetamol is above 20 mg/L or ALT/AST is abnormal.
Presentation after 24 hours: give acetylcysteine while awaiting results if symptomatic, paracetamol is detectable or transaminases are raised.
Activated charcoal 50 g for an acute potentially hepatotoxic ingestion presenting early (ideally within 1 hour) if the airway is safe.

sections.title: Acetylcysteine regimens
items: Deliver at least 300 mg/kg IV over the first 20 to 24 hours (US/Canada consensus). Infuse any 150 mg/kg loading dose over at least 1 hour. Dose on actual weight capped at 100 kg (US) or 110 kg (UK).
21-hour 3-bag regimen: 150 mg/kg over 1 hour, then 50 mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours.
12-hour SNAP regimen (UK, recognised by TOXBASE): 100 mg/kg over 2 hours, then 200 mg/kg over 10 hours; similar protection with fewer anaphylactoid reactions and less vomiting.
2-bag regimen: 200 mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours.
Level at or above the 300 mg/L line or massive ingestion: many toxicologists increase the acetylcysteine dose, but the US/Canada consensus sets no fixed dose. Discuss with a toxicologist.
Haemodialysis plus acetylcysteine if paracetamol is 900 mg/L or more with acidosis or altered consciousness (US/Canada consensus). Routine fomepizole is not recommended.

Anaphylactoid reaction (flushing, itch, wheeze, hypotension): pause the infusion for 30 minutes, give chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and salbutamol if wheezy, then restart at a slower rate. It is not a contraindication to further acetylcysteine.

sections.title: Stopping criteria
items: Near the end of the infusion recheck paracetamol, ALT/AST, INR and creatinine.

Stop when paracetamol is below 10 mg/L and ALT/AST are normal. If transaminases were raised, continue until they are falling (25 to 50% from peak), INR is below 2 and the patient is clinically well (US/Canada consensus).
If criteria are not met, continue acetylcysteine at the rate of the final infusion (for example 100 mg/kg over 16 hours) and recheck.
With hepatotoxicity monitor glucose (hypoglycaemia), INR, lactate, pH, phosphate and creatinine at least daily.

sections.title: Liver failure and referral
items: Discuss early with a liver unit if INR is rising, or there is encephalopathy, acidosis, rising creatinine, high lactate or hypoglycaemia.
King's College criteria for transplant referral: arterial pH below 7.30 after resuscitation, OR all of INR above 6.5, creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL (300 micromol/L) and grade 3 or 4 encephalopathy.
Do not give FFP to correct INR unless bleeding; INR is a key prognostic marker.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Pregnancy: assess and treat as for other adults; acetylcysteine is indicated. UK practice uses booking weight for the toxic dose and current weight for the drug dose.
Chronic alcohol use, malnutrition or enzyme-inducing drugs: use the same treatment line (the UK removed the separate high-risk line in 2012).
Low body weight (below 40 kg) or IV paracetamol overdose: seek poisons centre advice.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Plotting a level taken before 4 hours, or using the nomogram after a staggered or unknown-time ingestion.
Delaying acetylcysteine beyond 8 hours while waiting for a level.
Stopping acetylcysteine at a fixed time without checking stopping criteria.
Confusing units: 1 mg/L is about 6.6 micromol/L.

drugs.name: Acetylcysteine (21-hour, 3-bag)
drugs.dose: 150 mg/kg IV over 1 hour, then 50 mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours
drugs.notes: Weight capped at 100 kg (US) or 110 kg (UK). Extend at the final rate if stopping criteria are not met.

drugs.name: Acetylcysteine (SNAP, 12-hour)
drugs.dose: 100 mg/kg IV over 2 hours, then 200 mg/kg over 10 hours
drugs.notes: Fewer anaphylactoid reactions; used in UK practice.

drugs.name: Acetylcysteine (2-bag)
drugs.dose: 200 mg/kg IV over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours
drugs.notes: Alternative regimen delivering 300 mg/kg over 20 hours.

drugs.name: Activated charcoal
drugs.notes: Early acute ingestion with a safe airway.

drugs.name: Chlorphenamine
drugs.notes: Anaphylactoid reaction to acetylcysteine; pause the infusion for 30 minutes.
